A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, determine which represented billed revenue (invoices) is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant contractual conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with source-native identifiers and invoice metadata.

universe_scope.sources: authoritative files in this data room only
exclusions: non-authoritative or inferred sources outside the data room
expired statements of work treated as active contracts

world_eligible: invoice exists with id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status as appearing in sources
contract exists with identifier as appearing in sources

contract document contains textual clauses (consent/notice on change of control; termination on change of control; consent/notice before assignment including affiliate-only or competitor-prohibition variants)
contract or statement-of-work temporal status (e.g., expired vs not expired) derivable from source dates/terms
billed name and contract counterparty are distinct referents until joined
purpose_analytical: whether a contract counts as active for this purpose (expired SOW is not active)
whether a clause type is acquisition-relevant under the purpose definition
whether an invoice qualifies for inclusion (represented billed revenue tied to a counterparty with an active contract bearing acquisition-relevant conditions)
whether invoice-to-contract/counterparty association is confident enough to assert vs must remain unresolved

epistemic_requirements: Ground assertions in authoritative source files only; do not treat missing identity as a negative contractual finding.
When a billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, record association as unresolved rather than omitting the invoice or asserting a join.
Report identifiers (invoice_id, contract_id, billed_name) exactly as they appear in sources.
Distinguish absence of evidence for sameness from evidence of distinctness or non-qualification.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: invoice revenue is represented but link to the governing contract/counterparty is not confidently established

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: include every invoice that qualifies under purpose policy (active contract with acquisition-relevant condition) or that must be reported with unresolved association when identity join is required but not confident
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: for each included invoice, populate amount, currency, period, status from sources; contract_id when association is asserted or as best available when unresolved policy applies
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: do not emit closed-world negatives for missing identity; unresolved is the explicit non-assertion state

acquisition_relevant_conditions: require consent or notice on a change of control
permit termination upon a change of control
require consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: an expired statement of work is not an active contract
purpose_specific_policies.association_threshold: assert association only when billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently associated; otherwise association must be unresolved
purpose_specific_policies.inclusion_rule: a row appears when represented billed revenue is tied (asserted or unresolved) to a counterparty whose active contract contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition
not_world_truth: active-contract determination for diligence exposure (vs raw contract dates)

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, reconcile customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts: for each commercially relevant name or record, report whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records, is confidently distinct, or remains unresolved.

universe_scope.sources: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.entities: every commercially relevant name or record needed to connect CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates for a relationship

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_eligible: source-native records exist in CRM, billing, registry, and contract files with the identifier forms above
pairs of records are comparable candidates for identity linkage (same relationship thread: CRM account, billed name, governing contract, registry legal entity)
observable name strings and registry legal names as recorded in sources
purpose_analytical: SAME_ENTITY: confident judgment that two records denote the same legal counterparty
DISTINCT: confident judgment that two records denote different legal counterparties
UNRESOLVED: identification cannot be confidently resolved either way
mechanical normalization of exact legal-form variants of the same registered name vs rejection of merge based on superficial similarity alone

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical sameness.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Permit explicit unresolved identity; missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (DISTINCT) judgment.
Ground each link judgment with evidence from authoritative sources.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: identity relationship between left and right referents cannot be confidently classified as SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
completeness_expectations.pair_orientation: emit directed left/right pairs per schema; cover the connectivity graph needed for downstream joins
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: DISTINCT only when confidently distinct; absence of sameness evidence defaults to UNRESOLVED not DISTINCT

purpose_specific_policies.merge_policy: similarity of names alone is insufficient for SAME_ENTITY
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_sameness: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be merged mechanically
purpose_specific_policies.trade_name_caution: similar trade names across distinct registry entities do not imply sameness
purpose_specific_policies.required_connectivity: links must span CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidate dimensions for each commercial relationship thread
not_world_truth: global canonical identity of counterparties across systems
which pairs are commercially relevant to link (relationship-thread scope)

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under a joint test of current commercial relationship and qualifying contractual obligations, using Purpose B identifier forms.

universe_scope.sources: authoritative files in this data room only
exclusions: expired contracts as sources of current dependency
one-off paid historical invoices without an active qualifying contract

required_output_shape.identifier_forms: same as Purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)

world_eligible: invoice open/closed or paid status as recorded in sources
contract active/expired status and term structure (auto-renewal, rolling term, exclusivity language) as recorded in sources
contract_id and counterparty referents linkable when identity is resolved
which invoices are open vs settled one-off historical
purpose_analytical: current commercial relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
commercial dependency: BOTH current relationship AND at least one obligation kind (exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term)
dependent vs unresolved status when identity join is insufficient
active contract for dependency (excludes expired; excludes dependency from lone historical paid invoice without active contract)

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report dependency status as unresolved rather than false (not dependent).
Reuse Purpose B identifier conventions for counterparty referents.
Ground obligation-kind classifications and relationship currency in contract and invoice source text/fields.
Do not infer non-dependency from unresolved identity.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: dependency cannot be asserted because required invoice–contract–counterparty identity join is unresolved or current-relationship/obligations cannot be confidently assessed

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: emit a dependency row for each contract/counterparty thread that is dependent or must be reported unresolved when joins block assessment
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: populate open_invoice_ids from source invoice ids; obligation_kinds from detected qualifying clause types; counterparty and contract_id per identifier policy
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: do not emit dependent=false; non-dependency is absence of row or unresolved when evidence is insufficient

purpose_specific_policies.dependency_conjunction: commercial dependency requires BOTH (1) current commercial relationship AND (2) qualifying obligation in the active contract
current_relationship_criteria: active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
exclusions: expired contracts do not create current dependency
one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create current dependency
purpose_specific_policies.identity_dependency: relies on Purpose B identity links; unresolved identity forces status unresolved not dependent
not_world_truth: definition of current commercial relationship for diligence
which clause patterns count as exclusivity, auto_renewal, or rolling_term under this analytical frame
